summary: A Testbook web page presents a multiple-choice C question from the ISRO Scientist CS 2017 paper about a for loop that declares a shadowing local variable i inside its body. The loop variable i runs 0 to 4, but the inner int i = 10 is re-initialized on every pass, so the program prints 10 five times, with the answer marked as option 2 (10 10 10 10 10). The rest of the page is site navigation, exam listings, related question lists, and contact details, which are boilerplate.
one_line: Testbook quiz on C scoping: a loop body's local int i = 10 shadows the loop counter, so the program prints 10 five times.
key_facts: The question asks for the output of a C program with a for loop running i from 0 while i<5.
Inside the for loop body, the code declares a new variable 'int i = 10;' which shadows the loop counter.
The program calls printf("%d", i) inside the loop body, printing the local i.
The local i is incremented by i++ after printing, but it is re-declared and reset to 10 on each iteration.
The loop body runs 5 times, so the printed output is 10 10 10 10 10.
The question was previously asked in the ISRO Scientist CS 2017 Official Paper - I.
The answer options are: 10 11 12 13 14; 10 10 10 10 10; 0 1 2 3 4; and Compilation error.
The solution explains that the local variable i is inside the for loop, so its values are not the loop counter values 0 through 4.
The page is hosted by Testbook Edu Solutions Pvt. Ltd. and is listed under the Programming in C topic, While Loop subtopic.
The page notes that the ISRO Scientist CS 2022 notification was scheduled for November 29, 2022, with applications from November 29 to December 19, 2022.
The solution text describes the ISRO Scientist CS recruitment as requiring B.E./B.Tech. graduates in computer science and engineering.
